_about: The gaps the gauntlet asserts. Each row is one component, the verified vault file it is held
against, the figure read off that file's frames in vault/SPECS.md, and a measurement of the
app's own specimen that has to come out the same way.
A row without `assert` is honest about being a caution or a counter-example: the sheet shows
it, the run prints it, and nobody is allowed to call it a pass.
test/gauntlet.test.mjs refuses a row naming a file the eye never verified, a component that
is not in the registry, or a figure that is not the one SPECS.md measured.
A row carries `referenceRelation`. `informs` means the record is in this component's own for-list in
vault/SPECS-FOR.json -- the picture informs the drawing -- and `test/gauntlet.test.mjs` refuses the
row otherwise. `origin` means the picture is where the DEMAND was first measured, and makes no claim
that it informs this drawing; such a row carries `originClaim` saying how it entered, and it is never
coverage for the component. The distinction exists because de-quoting a component from a record has to
be allowed to coexist with a row that was honestly born from reading that record.

gaps.gap: In the audio editor the waveform exists as ink along a named lane and the ONLY thing that moves is a marker crossing an axis already fully drawn — ruler, labels and selection block hold still. A component that grows its own series into being is animating the data instead of reading it, so the library's series must arrive and then hold.

gaps.referenceFigure: measured: 48 frames over 8.0s, motion amplitude (max difference from frame zero): 5.4
gaps.gap: The audio editor's whole idiom is a marker crossing a strip that is ALREADY ink: the waveform, the ruler, the track labels and the selection block hold still and one hairline travels. `tape` has no such marker — it stamps `count`, `elapsed`, `still` and one refusal, and nothing translates along its axis. The five mark kinds that exist cannot express it: `trace` reveals a shape, `count` reveals by index, `cycle` addresses a clock, `level` is an extent from an anchor. Building it means a kind that moves a marker along an axis, which is a library change, not a showcase change.
gaps.notHeld: Two facts, read out of the source rather than the name. `tape` is the DECISION tape -- a queue of waits with an `elapsed` clock on each row and no axis to cross, so there is no position for a marker to have. And the component that DOES draw time, `river`, scales every lane to its own first-and-last event (px(t) normalises by that lane's span), so there is no shared present anywhere in the drawing to put a line on; a now-line clamped to each lane's right edge would say 'now is where this lane stopped', which is the falsest sentence a time chart can make. The idiom needs a shared absolute axis, which the library does not draw.

gaps.originClaim: The slot-geometry invariant was measured across 22 observations of this board: the left edge never moves and nothing re-sorts. dispatch came OUT of this record's for-list because its only relation to the board was the word `dispatch`, and that name-resemblance is on record as rejected -- so this row is the borrowed geometry claim, and the row is NOT coverage for dispatch.
gaps.referenceFigure: measured: 32 frames over 4.01s, motion amplitude (max difference from frame zero): 15.82
gaps.gap: On the Solari board only the cells whose value changed flip; the destination labels and the column heads never stir, so the movement is the report and everything else is ink. A dispatch panel that animates its own furniture on every refresh says 'everything changed' when one row did, so the furniture must hold still over a change.

gaps.originClaim: This record's display is where `a wait with no terminus gets no bar` was measured. Its for-list names killmail, hardCut and tape; collar is not among them -- collar refuses a countdown on an absent deadline, which is the same argument these frames make about a different component.
gaps.gap: a wait with no deadline drawn as a measured extent, a percentage, or a remaining-time figure — the claim "this much is left" made from no measurement. The reference states an unknown wait in words and draws nothing measurable.
gaps.referenceFigure: 24 frames over 4.0s, median delay 170.0ms, loop no return to frame zero
gaps.observed: asserted against `collar`, which has no deadline parameter at all and so draws a hatched area reading NO DEADLINE SET under REMAINING. The row was first filed against `dispatch`, which draws a fitted-parts chain and has no wait in it — named by resemblance instead of by drawing, the error class `scanOverlay` and `twoState` taught in the same week. Recorded here rather than quietly retargeted.
gaps.watch: a level/extent mark or a percentage or ETA appearing in the REMAINING region; a blank area replacing the hatched one

gaps.gap: the unmeasured ground shifting under the survey that never covered it. On the reference the plate's furniture is untouched by the animation while the return moves; a gap that shifts reads as a quantity, and a gap drawn from an absence must sit exactly where the survey says it sits.
gaps.referenceFigure: the plate and its legend are untouched by the animation
gaps.observed: asserted against the hatched ground rather than a legend: `coverage` draws no graticule and no colour key, so the reading's demand lands on the one element that exists to hold an absence — the dashed, hatched `UNMEASURED / terrain unrendered` block, which is `still`-stamped and must not translate while the contours arrive. Correcting the reading matters here: demanding an untouched legend from a component with no legend would be the `mfd` mistake in a new costume.
gaps.watch: the dark ground translating or scaling while contours sweep; a mark appearing on the hatch; contours drawing over the hatched area instead of stopping at it
